(6) Numbers reproduced independently with numpy over native samples [220500, 6615000) of the accepted run. Welch N=16384 periodic Hann with 390 frames gives source 20-45 = -57.151, denoised -59.386, processed -59.414 and cleaned -57.354 dB. All six bands for all four stage files match tone-ab.json to 3 decimals.

(6) Region frames 145 x 44100 = 6,394,500, and 6,394,500 // 16384 = 390. Excerpt length 15 x 44100 = 661,500. FFmpeg ebur128 over the region reads source -21.1, denoised -21.3 and cleaned -17.9 LUFS, consistent with the loudnorm input_i values -21.16, -21.33 and -17.96.

The actual-run tone-ab.json (sha256 2736e3d3...) was produced by script ab900835 (commit b8b3007), not HEAD. I diffed b8b3007..HEAD scripts/tone_ab.py: the only changes are exact_directory, the finalize reserve and the descriptor text. There are no numeric changes, so the measured values still stand.

The actual-run receipt JSON's `tests` block is stale: it records 26 tests and script_sha256_under_test d7de5596 (b8b64b5), while HEAD has 28 tests. The lane summary also gives two different test durations, 176.98 s and 400 s. Neither affects correctness.

Listening bias risk not called out in the receipt. The excerpt pairs use only the region-wide static gains, which matches the frozen spec ('excerpt LUFS informational; not re-matched'). Even so, per-excerpt informational LUFS differ X vs Y by 1.00 LU (pair 1: -19.88 vs -20.88), 0.44 LU (pair 2) and 0.79 LU (pair 3). A louder arm can be heard as 'fuller'. The receipt .md should tell the operator before blind listening.

Wording in the receipt's inference section (tone_ab-20261006T120702Z-actual-run.md): it says 'the 20-45 Hz mixture share falls 3.40 dB'. The -3.40 value is the matched-level delta; the share_db delta is -3.61. The lane summary also leaves out the -0.06 dB delivery-normalization term when splitting -3.40 into -2.07 and -1.28.

Durability: the six operator-listening excerpts and the trial render live only in the gitignored worktree directory .local/sprint2/tone_ab/artifacts/s2/tone_ab/20261006T041633Z-990aa1bd6737-20261006T120702Z/. Removing the worktree after merge will lose them. Root should relocate them or record their sha256 before cleanup. The receipt JSON does record the hashes.

The finalize reserve has a gap. The success path runs snapshot(run_dir) again after the work deadline, re-hashing every run-dir file including the two 230 MB .mov files in export/ (about 650 MB in total), and nothing bounds that step. If measurement ends close to the work deadline on a contended host, the re-hash plus write can take longer than the 10 s reserve. tool_api would then kill the process, leaving only a .partial-* staging dir and no failure record. The claim holds for FFmpeg overruns only. The pre-run snapshot is also unbounded by the deadline.

(3) Claim classes are acceptable. Measured values come with denominators (4/4, 5/5 arms, 30/30 bands, 215/215/219 and 482/482/495, 3/3, 1/1, 13/13, 15/15). Stage attribution and the NR8 comparison are labelled class I. Listening is empty (class L pending). attack_identity is 'unverified'. There are no note-correctness or missed-note claims. The trial is rejected_or_unreviewed_trial with adopted false and forwarded_to_profile false. eq_floor decision is root_and_operator_review_required. No default, profile or detector is adopted. The receipt withholds blind_key.

(5) Doctrine: there is no high-pass or notch anywhere. The only filter is the preregistered lowshelf f=100 g=1.5 trial on a separate f32 file. All 15 unknown fields are present with reasons. timeout_seconds is an integer 1..1800, each child runs under min(120 s, remaining) with ffprobe capped at 60 s, and the setup region 0-5 s is refused (start must be >= 5.0).
must_fix: The protected-output check is case-sensitive, but APFS on this host is case-insensitive, so the 'never writes into accepted run dirs / artifacts/runs/*' invariant can be bypassed. The check is scripts/tone_ab.py:347-352 (is_protected_location, which uses `path.is_relative_to(directory)` and the literal match parts[i]=='artifacts' and parts[i+1]=='runs'), applied at lines 994-999. Reproduction on a synthetic fixture in the scratchpad: run_dir=<S>/artifacts/runs/AcceptedRun, output_dir=<S>/Artifacts/runs/acceptedrun/probe-out. The check passed. The tool then created `.probe-out.partial-*` (trial WAV, excerpts, attack-positions.json) inside the run dir, the post-run readback failed with protected_input_changed, and `probe-out.failed/` was left permanently inside the 'accepted' run dir. On the real host, a read-only probe confirmed that is_protected_location(Path('/Users/jess/git/video-utils/Artifacts/runs/20261006t041633z-990aa1bd6737/x').resolve(), [run_dir]) returns False, while that path's parent exists. Exposure is CLI --output-dir only; the descriptor has no output field. Fix: compare by inode, i.e. walk output's existing ancestors with os.path.samefile / (st_dev, st_ino) against each protected dir and against the artifacts/runs dir, or casefold the comparison. Add a regression test with a case-variant output path.
